## Held-out canon scoring (PC72, tuned on / held out / matched)

*Two scores per row, outcome and route kept apart. **Diagnostic**: a mechanism family predicts the effect sentence and delivery carrier, compared with the evidence-labelled sentence (`HP_POTION_SENTENCES`, each citing an evidence row; no label is derived from a title). Outcome = verb, object and target agree; route = carrier agrees. **Engine**: the fitted mechanism is built into a brew dose case (`src/brew_heldout_cases.js`) and run through the generic case runner; the label, read in world terms, is the `expect`. Engine outcome = the world term the label names changed (mind rows are checked on the mood faculty, a fixed dial) (vitality quantity up or down, form property, mind property) after an oral dose; engine route = the mechanism's route leaves the dose where the label's route needs it. Self versus touched is not an engine distinction (the target is a bound holder), so engine outcome does not test it. The tuning sample never counts as held out. The split rule lives in `src/brew_heldout.js`; this section is generated.*

### hp_potions

| Held-out matches | Held out | Diagnostic outcome | Diagnostic route | Engine outcome | Engine route |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before the three title-pattern fixes | 17 | 10 | 10 | 13 (0 cannot run) | 12 (0 cannot run) |
| After the fixes (all held-out rows) | 17 | 11 | 11 | 15 (0 cannot run) | 13 (0 cannot run) |
| After, without the three rule-informed rows | 14 | 10 | 9 | 13 (0 cannot run) | 11 (0 cannot run) |

- **Read this carefully**: the three rows `mandrake_restorative_draught`, `skele_gro`, `dr_ubbly_s_oblivious_unction` were scored, found to be misses caused by a wrong title pattern, and then informed a rule (`scripts/b_coverage_ledgers.mjs`: the mandrake-restorative entry left the plant pattern, `skele-gro` moved to body-form, and dressing nouns such as unction and salve now precede the mind words). They stay in the held-out count but are not untouched; the next wave's held-out number must not be read as if they were. The last line above leaves them out.
- **Body-surface route (proposal, wave 3)**: the brew dose law gained `apply`, a preparation put on a named surface of a body for a contact time. The surface must exist on that body (a `surface:<name>` world mark); a fraction min(1000, uptake permille a minute x minutes) of the applied units reaches the body's dose account and the rest stays as surface residue in the account `coat` and splash already use. Defaults with their reasons: skin 40 a minute (a slow barrier), hair 100 (a large wet surface takes a treatment in about ten minutes), wound 250 (no barrier). A method's `uptakePermille` is the dial; the held-out route run uses 5 contact minutes for every row. Before it (wave 2): engine route 12 of 17 with 5 rows unable to run. Five rows now run the labelled route (`Label route runs`): four through `apply` on a body (swelling_solution, murtlap_essence and dr_ubbly_s_oblivious_unction on skin, sleekeazy_s_hair_potion on hair, surfaces read from evidence HPPE024, HPPE054, HPPE121 and HPPE062) and dragon_dung_fertiliser through `coat` on soil, a thing (HPPE124). Whether a potion is applied or drunk stays a design choice: the four body rows still miss on route because the fitted body-door and body-form defaults say potion.
- **Tuned on** (4): blood_replenishing_potion (body-door, HPPE058); calming_draught (mind-state, HPPE061); deflating_draught (body-form, HPPE025); doxycide (plant-or-creature-target, HPPE060). Engine on the tuning rows, reported apart: outcome 4 of 4, route 3 of 4.
- **Fitted defaults**: body-door: add vitality self via potion; mind-state: transform mind self via potion; body-form: transform form self via potion; plant-or-creature-target: remove vitality touched via spray. No default for conceal-or-sense (no evidence-labelled row).
- **Rule saw these rows** (title override set against evidence; not held out): Wolfsbane Potion. Out of the five mechanisms (not counted): Felix Felicis (luck-field).
- **Held out** (17): cure_for_boils, dr_ubbly_s_oblivious_unction, dragon_dung_fertiliser, draught_of_living_death, draught_of_peace, mandrake_restorative_draught, murtlap_essence, pepperup_potion, polyjuice_potion, potion_for_dreamless_sleep, shrinking_solution, skele_gro, sleekeazy_s_hair_potion, sleeping_draught, swelling_solution, veritaserum, wit_sharpening_potion.
- **Unscorable, missing data queued**: rows with no evidence-labelled sentence cannot be scored, since a title is the thing predicted. Per mechanism: body-door 46, effect-sentence 33, mind-state 31, plant-or-creature-target 31, body-form 23, conceal-or-sense 9, object-surface 8, place-release 6, luck-field 2, protection-field 2. The wiki body of each (revision in its `source`) is the queued data; the wiki host refused automated reads on 2026-11-13.

### hp_spells

- **Finding: every computed case is bespoke per row.** All 111 computed cases (108 scenes in `HP_CASE_SCENES` plus 3 case modules on exception rows) are keyed by the row id, and each case's sentence is that row's own truth (`caseSentence(row)` reads `row.truth`, which is the label). 26 are custom `build` functions and 82 are plain scene objects, 47 of them through the shared templates `carried`, `marked`, `unmarked`, `reshaped`, `measured`, `loss` or `treatment` (the shapes are general; every holder, destination and mark is authored for the row). None of the 111 is a held-out test. The pack's `intent` field also reproduces the truth sentence through `sentenceFromIntent` for all 108 rows, so it is the label in disguise and is not an input. The held-out set is what the identity rule can predict without having seen the row, and the engine score runs a fresh generic probe (`src/spell_heldout_cases.js`), never a scene.

| Held-out matches | Held out | Verb and object | Outcome (verb, object, direction) | Targeting | Time | Whole sentence | Engine outcome |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All held-out rows | 99 | 33 | 33 | 22 | 26 | 9 | 13 (82 cannot run) |
| Without the 58 rows whose intent only that row uses | 46 | 13 | 13 | 12 | | | |

- **Split rule** (`src/spell_heldout.js`): Among rows whose label is evidence-backed (no effectSource naming an authored ruling or reading) and that are not in a reserved family, the first row by id in each of the six families is the tuning sample; every other evidence-labelled row is held out.
- **Tuned on** (6): apparition (move, B6 pp3321-3324); anti-apparition (defend, B5 pp2771-2772); alarm (see, B7 pp4180–4182); blasting (make, B7 p3981); anapneo (mind, B6 p3018); lock (access, B5 p2737). Diagnostic on the tuning rows, reported apart: outcome 2 of 6, targeting 2; engine outcome 1 of 6.
- **Rule**: identity (roots and the English name words) -> intent (`inferIntent` over the tuning corpus plus the blind gloss lexicon `docs/gm/dispatch/foundation-s-2026-11-12/evidence/blind_root_lexicon.json`, written from word strings and the intent list only) -> verb, object, direction from `INTENT_LAW` -> target and time from the tuning rows sharing the intent (else all tuning rows) -> the grammar's own checks. The family field is never read. The hand-written `HP_ROOT_LEXICON` is not used: it maps roots to the rows' own intents.
- **Leak, stated**: `INTENT_LAW` has an entry coined for each of 58 intents that exactly one row uses (EF2), and the blind reader saw the intent list, so a correct guess on such a row gets its sentence by construction. The second table line leaves those rows out. This wave cannot show the law predicting an effect it was not written for; it shows how far identity alone reaches. Not comparable to the leave-one-out GL2 line (33 of 80 verb and object): that fit trains on 79 rows, this one on 6.
- **Outcome** = verb, object and direction agree; **targeting** = target agrees (the spell's carrier is the wand on every row, so carrier is not scored). Time is mostly an authored or inferred default in the pack notes and stays out of the headline.
- **Engine**: the predicted sentence is landed on a probe built from fixed dials for its world-term class (position, vitality, form, mark-add, mark-drop); the label, read in world terms, is the `expect`. The probes are validated by running each class on its own label (39 of 39 evidence-labelled rows with a template run and match). Targeting is not an engine distinction (the target is a bound holder), so no engine targeting score. "Cannot run" is a prediction or a label whose object has no generic probe, never forced.

### gu_kinds

- **Finding: the engine runs only authored abilities.** 18 of 53 held-out kinds carry an activation row (its effect, pool and charge are built from the scene's `observed` text and an `authored` quantity), so 47 cannot run an engine probe (no activation row, or no class predicted, or no probe effect for the class). The 5 refinement recipes are not scored: each names its own ingredients and stages by hand, and no rule predicts a stage list. A run needs a blind name lexicon (as the spell split used) before the rule can move this score.

| Held-out matches | Held out | Diagnostic outcome (function class) | Engine outcome (effect class) | Engine route (pool and charge) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All held-out kinds | 53 | 4 | 1 of 6 (47 cannot run) | 4 of 6 |

- **Split rule** (`src/gu_heldout.js`): Among catalogue kinds whose parts row names a function, kinds are ordered by an FNV-1a hash of "gu-heldout-1:<id>" and the first 8 are the tuning sample; every other such kind is held out. Dial: seed and sample size (a different seed is a different split, and the fixed one is the reported one).
- **Tuned on** (8): fire-source, light-source, lightning-eye, moon-scar, nine-eyes-liquor-worm, starlight-firefly, stealth-scales, vitality-grass. On the tuning kinds, reported apart: diagnostic outcome 8 of 8.
- **Out of scope** (20): kinds with no function reading in the catalogue.
- **Rule**: class votes from wiki type and path labels and name words seen on the tuning kinds (ties alphabetical); pool from the wiki rank (6 and up immortal, else primeval); charge from the tuned rank band, else the tuned mode. The probe ability is the plainest effect of the predicted class, run through `resolveGuActivation`. Outcome and route are separate. No rule was changed after scoring, so there is no untouched-subset line.

## Row format

```json
{"id": "stealth-scales", "source": "gu-identity-evidence.json#stealth-scales; ch. 127", "state": "runs-canon", "mechanisms": ["G", "L"], "test": "tests/gu_catalogue.test.js", "note": ""}
```

- `state`: `runs-canon`, `runs-authored`, `runs-derived`, `blocked:<rule>`, `not-a-thing:<reason>` or `unclassified` (CV2). Rules and reasons are short slugs, such as `blocked:PGB2` or `not-a-thing:alias`.
- `runs-derived` and `expressed-derived` (PWC20): the value comes from a world rule, not a source that states it, and the row carries `derived: {"rule": "<rule id>", "inputs": [...]}`. The runs share counts canon and authored only, so derivation shows apart.
- A `runs-*` row names an existing test file in `test` (optionally `#test name`).
- `catalogued` is a typed state for identity parts with a source and no executed effect. `expressed-*` is computed by the runner; a row carrying `case` is the one place it is typed, because the runner checks it there.
- `case`: optional `{"module": "<repo-relative js>", "id": "<case id>"}`; the module exports `coverageCase(id)` (shape in the header of `scripts/coverage_report.mjs`). `check:coverage` fails when a typed state disagrees with the computed one, a case module is missing or lacks the export, or a case throws.
- `mechanisms`: the owners the thing appears on (SC4), by chat letter or owner name.
